facts.raw_span: A 56-year-old nulliparous woman presented 14 months after a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas
normal Pap smear
no chest radiograph or endometrial biopsy was obtained
an 18–20-week–size uterus (1518 g) was removed via prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
superficial pelvic endometriosis was noted and cauterized
weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma
left lower quadrant pain, persistent cough, and shortness of breath
firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex
multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest
poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma
A 56-year-old nulliparous woman presented 14 months after a supracervical laparoscopic hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy
menorrhagia, pelvic pain, and large uterine leiomyomas
normal Pap smear
no chest radiograph or endometrial biopsy was obtained
an 18–20-week–size uterus (1518 g) was removed via prolonged mechanical morcellation without a containment bag
superficial pelvic endometriosis was noted and cauterized
weakly proliferative endometrium without atypia, adenomyosis, and leiomyoma
left lower quadrant pain, persistent cough, and shortness of breath
firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex
multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest
poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis
grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma

concepts.why: The patient's vaginal biopsy showed grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma, which is a type of cancer that arises from the endometrium.

The patient had superficial pelvic endometriosis noted and cauterized during her initial surgery, and now presents with a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex.

The core-needle biopsy of the left pelvic mass revealed poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis, which is consistent with a diagnosis of poorly differentiated carcinoma.
The patient has multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, and a vaginal biopsy showing grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma, which suggests metastatic disease.
The core-needle biopsy of the left pelvic mass revealed poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis, which could be consistent with a diagnosis of sarcoma.
The patient has multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest, which could be consistent with a diagnosis of lymphoma.
The patient's biopsy results show both epithelial and mesenchymal components, which is consistent with a diagnosis of carcinosarcoma.

The patient had superficial pelvic endometriosis noted and cauterized during her initial surgery, and now presents with a firm left lower quadrant abdominal mass and a fleshy lesion at the vaginal apex, which could be consistent with a diagnosis of endometrial stromal sarcoma.

rationales.F05: The use of mechanical morcellation without a containment bag may have contributed to the dissemination of endometrial tissue.
rationales.F06: The presence of superficial pelvic endometriosis suggests a possible link to the development of disseminated endometriosis.
rationales.F10: The presence of multiple hypermetabolic masses in the pelvis, abdomen, and chest suggests a possible metastatic process.
rationales.F11: The presence of poorly differentiated epithelioid cells with hyperchromatic nuclei in necrosis is more consistent with a poorly differentiated carcinoma than with endometrioid adenocarcinoma.
rationales.F12: The diagnosis of grade 3 endometrioid adenocarcinoma provides strong evidence for this condition.
